Topic: The Transformational View of Derivatives: From Slopes to Dynamic Rates

Target audience: University students (Calculus I beginners)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Review: The Static Slope

Lecture lines:
The secant line connects two distinct points.
Its slope is the ratio, rise over run.
Think of a hiker on a steep trail.

Planned animations:
Fade in text: The slope between two points A and B.
Draw a line segment connecting points A and B on a curve.
Label points A and B with color #FFFFFF.
Display the static formula for slope: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1).
Flash the formula in color #FFD700 to emphasize the definition.

Section: section_2 — The Concept of Transformation: Secant to Tangent

Lecture lines:
Shrink the interval between these two points.
The secant slides towards a single point.
It transforms into the tangent line.
Imagine a camera shutter speed becoming faster.
The 'blur' reveals the exact instant direction.

Planned animations:
Fade in text: As B approaches A, the secant becomes tangent.
Animate point B moving along the curve toward point A.
Update the secant line segment continuously as B moves.
Draw the limit tangent line as B reaches A.
Highlight the transition with color #00FF00 for the tangent line.

Section: section_3 — Defining the Derivative as a Dynamic Operator

Lecture lines:
The derivative is a dynamic transformation operator.
It maps position to its rate of change.
Like a chameleon's tongue, capturing instantaneous speed.
It transforms functions into their velocity graphs.
A micro-second map of the function's trend.

Planned animations:
Fade in text: The derivative is the instantaneous rate of change.
Display the formal limit definition of the derivative.
Animate the limit process symbols disappearing as the derivative exists.
Apply color #FF00FF to the f'(x) term.
Flash the entire formal definition for clarity.

Section: section_4 — Visualizing the 'Derivative Function' Graph

Lecture lines:
Visualize the original curve alongside its derivative.
The derivative's height equals the original slope.
A roller coaster's slope defines its speed.
The speedometer graph tracks the motion exactly.
Comparing curves reveals their fundamental link.

Planned animations:
Fade in text: Mapping slopes of tangent lines to points.
Show the original curve and the derivative graph side-by-side.
Draw tangent lines at different x-values on the original curve.
Map the slopes to new points on the derivative graph.
Connect the points to form the derivative function graph in #FFFF00.

Section: section_5 — Summary: The Power of Perspective

Lecture lines:
Derivatives connect local slopes to global behavior.
They allow predicting the path of rockets.
Every tiny transformation tells the whole story.

Planned animations:
Fade in text: Derivative represents the slope everywhere.
Display the original curve and derivative graph together.
Highlight key points on both graphs with #FFFFFF.
Show the relationship using a dashed line animation.
Fade out all elements to complete the summary.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
